decision: FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING — Frozen decision_rule condition C1 triggers: ALL three tested alphas (0.1, 0.5, 1.0) have |shuffled-action null_mean| >= 0.1 bits (0.240, 0.200, 0.275 respectively), each 2.0-2.75x above threshold. No alpha achieves both C1 and C3. Audit PASS confirms all recomputed metrics match producer. The bias is intrinsic to Laplace-smoothed histogram estimation: smoothing inflates H(Y|Z,A) more than H(Y|Z) because the (z,a) conditioning space has n_a times more cells, and Laplace pseudo-counts add artificial uncertainty proportional to cell count. Corrected P(z) denominator (audit V1) does not change the FALSIFIED verdict. The entropy-rate estimator has WORSE null centering than plug-in KL at high alpha (0.275 vs 0.064 at alpha=1.0). The deterministic SPA construct validation (B-ENTROPY-RATE-DEG) fails at alpha>=0.5 (negative CMI), confirming the bias is estimator-intrinsic, not data-intrinsic.

reason: The entropy-rate CMI hypothesis H1 is falsified: the per-stratum KL bias is NOT estimator-specific. Entropy-rate CMI, which computes H(Y|Z)-H(Y|Z,A) globally rather than summing per-stratum KL, exhibits the SAME irreconcilable tradeoff between sensitivity and null centering. The root cause is Laplace smoothing on discrete spaces with many cells — it adds artificial uncertainty that scales with cell count, and the (z,a) space has n_a times more cells than the z-only space. This closes the entropy-rate CMI pathway on this SPA class. The CMI estimation program on discrete SPAs with Laplace smoothing is now exhausted across plug-in KL (parent, alpha sweep), entropy-rate (this experiment), KSG CMI k=5 (parent, insensitive), and LR chi2 (parent, history collapse). The next orthogonal attack vectors are: (a) Bayesian model comparison, which does not use histogram smoothing; (b) likelihood-ratio tests between nested models; (c) non-smoothed estimators (KDE, kNN with bias correction, neural density estimators); (d) production Web data with continuous state representations. The Physics lane must pivot away from histogram-based discrete CMI estimation.
